title: We know sleep, exercise and diet are vital for health. But why?

paragraphs.en: For generations we’ve treated them as separate prescriptions – sleep restores us, exercise strengthens us and food fuels us. Yet neuroscience is beginning to suggest something rather more elegant: they’re all essentially doing the same job.
paragraphs.zh: 几代人以来，我们一直把它们当作各自独立的处方——睡眠让我们恢复精力，运动让我们强壮，食物为我们供能。然而神经科学开始提出一个更为精妙的观点：它们本质上在做同一件事。

paragraphs.en: What has changed is not the recommendations themselves, but our understanding of the biology beneath them. The more scientists study the brain, the clearer it becomes that cognition is astonishingly energy intensive. Although the brain makes up about 2% of body weight, it uses roughly a fifth of the body’s energy at rest. Every memory we retrieve, every decision we make and every creative insight carries a metabolic cost. Thought itself is an energy-hungry act.
paragraphs.zh: 发生变化的不是这些建议本身，而是我们对它们背后生物学机制的理解。科学家对大脑研究得越多，就越清楚地认识到认知是极其耗能的。虽然大脑约占体重的 2%，但它在静息状态下消耗了全身约五分之一的能量。我们检索的每一段记忆、做出的每一个决定、获得的每一点创意洞见，都要付出代谢成本。思考本身就是一种消耗能量的行为。

paragraphs.en: That raises an obvious question: where does all that energy come from? The answer lies deep in evolutionary history. More than 2bn years ago, a primitive cell engulfed a bacterium. Instead of being digested, the bacterium remained, forming a long-term partnership with its host.
paragraphs.zh: 这引出了一个显而易见的问题：所有这些能量从何而来？答案深藏在进化史之中。20 多亿年前，一个原始细胞吞噬了一个细菌。这个细菌没有被消化，而是留了下来，与宿主形成了长期的伙伴关系。

paragraphs.en: Over time, this arrangement became one of biology’s most important alliances. The bacterium became remarkably efficient at capturing the chemical energy stored in food and transforming it into ATP, the molecule that powers almost every biological process. The host offered protection, and together they made complex life possible.
paragraphs.zh: 随着时间推移，这种安排成为生物学最重要的同盟之一。这个细菌变得极其擅长捕获储存在食物中的化学能，并将其转化为 ATP——这种分子为几乎所有的生物过程提供能量。宿主提供保护，二者共同使复杂的生命成为可能。

paragraphs.en: Intelligence depends not simply on the brain’s wiring, but on the uninterrupted flow of energy through that wiring
paragraphs.zh: 智能不仅取决于大脑的神经连接，更取决于能量通过这些连接持续不断的流动。

paragraphs.en: That partnership is still running inside us today. Mitochondria – the descendants of that ancient bacterium – exist in almost every cell in the body. The exception is the mature red blood cell, which removes them to make space for haemoglobin and improve oxygen transport. Even here, biology reveals its logic: everything is shaped by trade-offs in energy efficiency.
paragraphs.zh: 这种伙伴关系至今仍在我们体内运转。线粒体——那个古老细菌的后代——存在于体内几乎每一个细胞中。唯一的例外是成熟的红细胞，它们会清除线粒体，为血红蛋白腾出空间，以改善氧气运输。即便是这里，生物学也揭示了它的逻辑：一切都是能量效率权衡的结果。

paragraphs.en: For decades, mitochondria were introduced in biology textbooks as the cell’s “powerhouses” – important, dependable but rather dull. The stars of the show were undeniably neurons. Today, that picture is changing.
paragraphs.zh: 几十年来，教科书一直把线粒体介绍为细胞的“发电厂”——重要、可靠但相当乏味。舞台上的主角无疑是神经元。如今，这幅图景正在改变。

paragraphs.en: We’re discovering that neurons produce thought, ideas and emotions only because mitochondria continuously transform fuel into the energy they need. Intelligence depends not simply on the brain’s wiring, but on the uninterrupted flow of energy through that wiring. This is a subtle shift in perspective, but an important one.
paragraphs.zh: 我们正在发现，神经元之所以能产生思想、想法和情感，正是因为线粒体不断把燃料转化为它们所需的能量。智能不仅取决于大脑的神经连接，更取决于能量通过这些连接持续不断的流动。这是一种微妙的视角转变，却至关重要。
